work_item: W1 -- does reduction order actually diverge on real hardware?
hardware: single node, 2x NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition, PCIe (topo=NODE), NO NVLINK; 72 CPU cores. torch 2.11.0+cu128.
design: Identical input BYTES at every configuration: leaf i's M-vector is a pure function of i, so nothing about the data changes when the job is reshaped -- only who holds which leaf and in what order the partial sums combine.
outcome: PARTIAL, exactly as the pre-registration anticipated and named in advance

reshape_axis.statement: EVERY world size produced a DIFFERENT 64-bit root, on identical inputs, for every one of the 12 (N, dtype, data-profile) cases. 14 of 14 distinct.

library_axis.swept: NCCL_ALGO in {Tree, Ring} x NCCL_PROTO in {LL, LL128, Simple}, plus default, at G=2
library_axis.statement: ONE root across all 7. This is structural, not an empirical null: at G=2 the cross-rank reduction is a single floating-point addition per element, which is commutative and exact whatever the schedule. No NCCL algorithm or protocol can move it on a 2-GPU node. Stated as such; not generalised to larger G.

repeatability.statement: run-to-run at a FIXED configuration is bitwise deterministic; the divergence is caused by reshape, not by noise. That decomposition is the point.

device_axis.statement: at a FIXED partition (G=2) the CPU and GPU roots also differ, because the local partial sum uses a different reduction tree on each device -- measured for all 12 cases, 0 agreements.

pairwise.fp64_cells: 34 configurations, 15 distinct roots, 441/561 = 78.6% of configuration pairs disagree
pairwise.fp32_cells: 21 configurations, 15 distinct roots, 189/210 = 90.0% of configuration pairs disagree

result.ranks_within_a_run: all ranks of every run agreed bitwise (0 intra-run disagreements)

controls.crosscheck_note: v002 and v003 are independent full re-runs of the gloo arm under two different result-bookkeeping harnesses: 168/168 cells identical. The harness change did not move a single measured bit.

not_reached.nccl_beyond_G2: NCCL with 3 ranks, and with 4 ranks sharing 2 GPUs, were attempted as declared-exploratory arms and BOTH FAILED (rc=1 / hang, 180 s timeout). NCCL requires one rank per device. Recorded as failures in W1/v003/index.json, not dropped. The library axis is therefore measured only at G=2 on this machine.
